note: Kling 4.0 director templates. {name} fields are filled by the code; [bracketed] slots are for the director. The master prompt follows template H's 15-header order; {timing} expands to one line per shot.
framings: Wide establishing frame, 84° diagonal FOV, lens at waist height, three-quarter angle
Medium shot, 47° FOV, lens at chest height
Close-up, 47° FOV, eye level, focus on the eyes
Insert on the key prop, 29° FOV
shot_line: {a}-{b}s — SHOT {n} — @loc_[place]_v1. {frame}, {move}. [ONE action and its physical consequence]. {end}
shot_end: Final image holds to the last frame.
master: SCENE CONTEXT
Block {index} of {total}. {duration} s, {ratio}. Story: {story}
[2-4 sentences: who, where, what happens in this block, how it ends, genre and mood.]
ACTIVE REFERENCES
@Image1 — CHARACTER — [NAME]: face, hair, build and wardrobe match the reference 100%. Reference controls identity only; backdrop, lighting and pose are not inherited.
@Image2 — LOCATION — [PLACE]: controls layout, materials and practical lights. The reference's camera angle and framing are not inherited.
@Image3 — STORYBOARD: follow its shot order and framing. Do not render the storyboard itself.
LOCATION MAP
[Geometry in metres, where each object sits, screen direction frame-left / frame-right, where the camera works from.]
FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
[What is in frame on frame 1: lens height, angle, who stands where.] Exactly 1 person in the shot.
FORMAT MODE
Controlled multi-shot sequence, {shots} shots, hard cuts between shots.
OPTICS
Close-ups 47°, medium-wide 63°, wide 84°, inserts 29°; anamorphic rectilinear character; lens locked within each shot; focus on the eyes at held moments.
CAMERA
Dolly and gimbal moves motivated by the action, at most two moves per shot.
ACTION TIMING
{timing}
ACTING TASK — [NAME]
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): [...]. MOTIVE: [...]. GOAL: [...]. OBSTACLE: [...].
TACTIC: [verbs aimed at the partner; the work happens in the eyes]. Gaze stays engaged in the task with a natural blink cadence.
PHYSICS
[Weight, cloth, smoke, dust and footfalls: how each object really behaves.]
LIGHTING
[Practical sources only: positions, colour temperature, what stays dark.]
AUDIO
English lines only, or silent acting with Arabic voice-over added in the edit. [Ambience; SFX timed to the action.] No music. No subtitles.
STYLE
[Genre look], fine film grain, natural skin texture with pores, one consistent grade.
QUALITY
Readable faces and hands at held moments; natural 180° shutter motion blur on fast moves; stable temporal continuity; consistent anatomy; each object stays one consistent object.
POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Exactly 1 person in every shot; [handedness]; [object sizes against known things]; screen direction stays frame-left to frame-right; [what the last frame shows].
storyboard: Create a 3x3 grid storyboard (nine equal panels, thin white borders, {ratio} overall, 2K) for a short film, block {index}. Story: {story}
References: Image 1 is [NAME] — keep the face, hair and wardrobe the same in every panel; Image 2 is the location.

Consistent practical lighting and grade across all panels: [light + palette]. Photorealistic film stills, anamorphic look with oval bokeh and horizontal flares, fine film grain, three-quarter angles, varied framing. Panels carry pictures only, free of text, numbers and captions.

settings.mode: Omni Reference (images, videos, elements) or Keyframes (images only); never both

plan.takes_plan: 2-4 takes per block; quote credits as takes x blocks and log each paid job in living-site tools/ledger.py before generating
plan.continuity: the last frame of block N becomes the first keyframe of block N+1
